options.label: System diagram as index
options.what: The five-part system (inputs, four trades, licence, market, afterlife) is the organiser; lectures and interactives hang off its boxes.
options.why: Make the case readable "whole" and let every piece point back to one model of a creative industry.
options.worked: Clear conceptual model; strong for reference and for reuse across other civilisation pages.
options.weaknesses: Judged "no coherent thread" in v1: an index is not a plot, the learner has no reason to go on.
requires: a hub page or diagram component
tagging every piece to a system box
conflicts: a single linear scroll as the only entry

options.label: Chronological chapters with motifs
options.what: Seven chapters in date order, held together by eight listed motifs (market, four hands, seal, price, blue, ban, export, icon).
options.why: One continuous thread in place of separate screens.
options.worked: Chronology is easy to follow; one real loop (learn the seal in ch. 3, use it in ch. 5).
options.weaknesses: Critique: "an index, not a plot"; protagonists drop after one chapter; timeline runs backwards inside chapters.

options.label: Five acts on five publishers' bets
options.what: Prologue plus five acts, each led by a publisher (Tsutaya, Eijudō, Uoya, Hayashi–Bing–Wright, the Bank of Japan) and a bet.
options.why: The research report's fix for v2: a named protagonist and stakes per act, payoffs across acts.
options.worked: Gives a dramatic question per act and recurring characters; survived into v4 unchanged.
options.weaknesses: v3 opened each segment with a prediction, which read as invasive; act content still dense in places.

options.label: Overture that tells the whole story, Coda that rebuilds it
options.what: A nine-shot scroll overture (paper, wave, shop, blocks, Edo, seal, sea, return, contents) before Act I; act Rebuilds and a Coda order-rebuild with a private guess ledger at the end.
options.why: The brief asked for an opening "3.5D" scrollytelling that tells the whole concept and for questions folded into the experience.
options.worked: Frames the thesis in under a minute; the Coda closes the loop and hands off to the Atlas.
options.weaknesses: Adds a long intro before content (skip link needed); heavy WebGL dependency with still fallback.

options.label: Single-column document
options.what: One long doc with tables.
options.why: Research capture and review.
options.worked: Complete and easy to edit with others.
options.weaknesses: Not a learning experience; no visuals.

options.label: Separate screens (hub + lecture player + tool pages)
options.what: A hub page, a lecture player with a dark stage and station list, and one page per interactive.
options.why: Prototype each learner surface separately on a canvas.
options.worked: Each screen is clear and focused; the lecture player is a recognisable pattern.
options.weaknesses: Judged "too complicated": many entry points and context switches.

options.label: Sticky stage beside a reading column
options.what: A dark map+timeline pane fixed beside a cream essay column.
options.why: Keep instruments visible while reading.
options.worked: Instruments always present.
options.weaknesses: Two products side by side; raster flashes cream into navy; both instruments live at once; 47 viewports of identical anatomy (critique).

options.label: One pinned stage, beats as cards over it
options.what: The stage fills the screen and shows one instrument at a time; short beat cards scroll over its left side; tools sit in the stage (in the beat card on phones).
options.why: Benchmarks: every award exemplar holds one instrument while short steps change its state.
options.worked: Full-bleed prints and maps; one instrument per beat; coherent with deep zoom.
options.weaknesses: Judged "components not grouped" and "small blocks with a question".

options.label: Pinned stage + scene sheets on an ink thread + full-screen rooms
options.what: Beats grouped into washi scene sheets with an ink thread; act openers as heroes; deep tools moved to full-screen rooms reached by links.
options.why: Answer "group components that make a set" and give tools room to breathe.
options.worked: Visible grouping; rooms let tools be full-size without breaking the scroll.
options.weaknesses: Two levels (story and rooms) to keep in sync; more chrome.
requires: room shell with focus trap and hash routes

options.label: Document headings
options.what: Numbered sections only.
options.why: Reference reading.
options.worked: Fine for a doc.
options.weaknesses: No wayfinding in an experience.

options.label: Hub with system-diagram filter and lens bar
options.what: Tap a system box and the lectures and interactives that touch it light up; lens pills (Time, Place, Movements, Objects) in the top bar.
options.why: Make the diagram the table of contents.
options.worked: Shows how pieces relate to the model.
options.weaknesses: Adds a choice before any content; judged too complicated.

options.label: Lecture station list with Previous/Next
options.what: A numbered station sidebar with progress and Previous/Next.
options.why: A familiar lecture-player pattern.
options.worked: Clear progress within a lecture.
options.weaknesses: Separate from the rest of the case.

options.label: Chapter dots + Explore toggle
options.what: Numbered chapter circles in the header; "Explore the Atlas" dims the story and hands over the map and timeline.
options.why: Give a free-exploration mode beside the story.
options.worked: Explore mode is a good idea that later versions kept.
options.weaknesses: Titles only on hover, no reading time or in-chapter progress; explore had nothing to click (critique).

options.label: Act numerals + live year/era + Explore
options.what: A slim bar with P I–V act links, the current year with its Japanese era, Explore, reduce-motion and theme.
options.why: Orientation in time at every step.
options.worked: Always know act and year; works on phones.
options.weaknesses: v3 lacked a way into tools or people outside the story.
requires: story steps that carry a year

options.label: Rooms menu, Cast deck and "Go deeper" links
options.what: A Rooms menu (Desks, Workshop, Views) with hash routes, a Cast deck that counts people met, and in-beat links into rooms.
options.why: Give depth without lengthening the scroll.
options.worked: Separates reading from doing; deep links shareable (#room-desks.censor).
options.weaknesses: More entry points again (risk of v1's complexity).

options.label: Globe/Map/List with world → region → unit tiers
options.what: Three views of the same data; breadcrumbs; URL tokens per state.
options.why: A hub across all F1 chapters.
options.worked: List view is complete and accessible; tokens make states linkable.
options.weaknesses: Hub only; does not teach by itself.

options.label: Prediction per lecture, check per interactive (specified)
options.what: Each lecture has one one-tap prediction and an argued station; each interactive ends with a one-tap check.
options.why: Learning evidence: predictions and retrieval.
options.worked: Clear pedagogical intent.
options.weaknesses: Unbuilt.

options.label: One-tap check cards (seal red)
options.what: Multiple-choice cards inside lectures and tools, answered by one tap with a verdict.
options.why: Quick retrieval inside tools.
options.worked: Cheap and clear.
options.weaknesses: v2: right/wrong by colour and strikethrough only, no live region; feels like a quiz bolted on.

options.label: Predict before each segment, decide after
options.what: A "Before you read: predict" card opens each of 9 segments; 7 decide checks follow.
options.why: Pre-questions prime attention (learning evidence).
options.worked: Systematic coverage.
options.weaknesses: Judged weird and invasive at chapter starts; readings became "small blocks with a question".
conflicts: an overture or act opener as first impression

options.label: Optional late guess answered on the instrument; ghost vs record
options.what: One optional prompt late in a scene: tap a place, drag a year, tap a mark, or slider/choice/bet; your answer is a hollow ghost and the record solid ink; nothing scored; scrolling past shows the record.
options.why: Fold questions into the experience instead of in front of it.
options.worked: Feels like part of the instrument; respects the no-points rule.
options.weaknesses: Only 9 in 71 beats; easy to miss.

options.label: Act Rebuild and Coda ledger
options.what: At each act end, place 4–6 tiles back on the timeline or map; the Coda rebuilds six items in order and shows your guesses against the record.
options.why: Retrieval practice without scores.
options.worked: Spaced retrieval with one tile from an earlier act.
options.weaknesses: Unmeasured; optional and skippable by design.
requires: tile placement on map and timeline

options.label: Framing question on the card
options.what: Units and lenses carry a guiding question shown on the card or lens caption.
options.why: Orient exploration without checks.
options.worked: Light and non-invasive.
options.weaknesses: No feedback loop.

options.label: Ten interactives as system joints (spec)
options.what: I1–I10 each with lens, data, action, meaning and check.
options.why: Design every interactive against the system.
options.worked: The spec set every later tool.
options.weaknesses: Unbuilt.

options.label: Standalone interactive pages
options.what: Read the margin (hotspots + dating), Before and after the ban (year scrubber), What a sheet cost (bars + cap line).
options.why: Prototype the joints of the system one by one.
options.worked: Margin and Cost carried forward.
options.weaknesses: Disconnected from narrative; 7 of 10 not built.

options.label: Eight widgets embedded in the scroll
options.what: Chain flowchart, margin, blue-route scrubber, three waves, price, ban, edition counter, export map, inline in beats.
options.why: Put each tool where the story needs it.
options.worked: Placement in the thread was right.
options.weaknesses: Judged primitive; four autoplay; timer bug overwrote the map; three meaningful ones dropped (critique).

options.label: Six stage tools
options.what: Peel, three waves, margin, edition, contract (read, not played), closing recall, rendered in the pinned stage.
options.why: Rebuild the meaningful tools to the case spec.
options.worked: Three waves with diagnostics and peel are solid.
options.weaknesses: Judged interactions primitive.

options.label: Lab modules with stage and room modes
options.what: Nine labs (print, compare, edition, contract, catalogue, seal timeline, censor, step into the view, uki-e box) behind one mount interface; compact in the stage, full in rooms.
options.why: Make tools feel crafted and give them space; absorb the Desks and Workshop side branches.
options.worked: Consistent workbench frame, sources, reset, keyboard paths; 3D only where space is the argument.
options.weaknesses: Biggest code surface (lazy chunks ~1.5 MB JS total).

options.label: Field notebook and ink hand-off
options.what: Inked marks, rumours and lenses practised, carried between artifacts in plain #ink tokens.
options.why: Knowledge as the save file (Atlas study).
options.worked: No points; works across separate artifacts.
options.weaknesses: Depends on learners finishing a unit.

options.label: None / state swaps
options.what: Static pages; state re-renders only.
options.why: Prototype speed.
options.worked: Fast to build.
options.weaknesses: Feels inert; v2 critique asked for animation.

options.label: Scroll-triggered flights + autoplay tools
options.what: Map flies per beat; tools autoplay for 4–5 s.
options.why: Make instruments respond to reading.
options.worked: Shows the instruments are alive.
options.weaknesses: No pause, no reduced motion, orphaned timers.

options.label: Scoped instrument transitions
options.what: Map scale changes, scripted map anims (fire, relocations), timeline lanes; every timer in a Scope; reduce-motion toggle.
options.why: Fix v2's timer bug and make motion meaningful.
options.worked: Reliable; nothing runs after its beat.
options.weaknesses: Still read as primitive.

options.label: Choreographed motion with tokens and 3D/2.5D
options.what: Duration and easing tokens, one primary motion per beat, ink-bleed reveals, multi-plane parallax, globe flights; reduced motion cuts to stills.
options.why: Stop interactions feeling primitive; space is the argument for the Wave and the views.
options.worked: Distinctive; still accessible.
options.weaknesses: WebGL cost and fallbacks to maintain.
requires: three.js stage with tiering and still fallback

options.label: Plain document
options.what: Doc typography.
options.why: Research record.
options.worked: Readable.
options.weaknesses: No visuals.

options.label: Paper, ink, Prussian blue; dark lecture stage
options.what: Paper #F4F2EC, ink, one blue accent, seal red for checks; dark stage so prints carry the light.
options.why: Let the prints be the colour.
options.worked: Restrained and legible.
options.weaknesses: Two moods (light hub, dark lecture).

options.label: Editorial cream column beside a navy dashboard
options.what: Serif display, cream column, navy map pane, seal red on every accent, 96×120 portrait crops.
options.why: Quick, clean template.
options.worked: Competent typography.
options.weaknesses: "Competent and placeless"; two products; seal red means nothing (critique).
conflicts: seal red reserved for the censor

options.label: Washi, sumi and indigo; seal red only for the censor
options.what: One ink-on-paper world: washi grounds, sumi line, indigo accent, seal red reserved for the censor and 1842; Shippori Mincho / Source Serif 4 / IBM Plex Sans; prints full-bleed.
options.why: Commit to one world (critique).
options.worked: Kept by the user as the visual direction (ARCH_V4.md).
options.weaknesses: v3 felt ungrouped; v4 adds materials (hanko, kraft, workbench frames) to group sets.

options.label: Dense reference prose
options.what: Full sentences with sources and confidence words, tables.
options.why: Capture everything once.
options.worked: Source of truth for content.
options.weaknesses: Not learner-facing.

options.label: Short station narration with claim ids
options.what: One or two sentences per station with claim ids.
options.why: Narrated lectures.
options.worked: Traceable claims.
options.weaknesses: Judged "lectures too thin".

options.label: Long essay paragraphs
options.what: 5,627 words in 33 beats; long sentences; "the course" voice.
options.why: Keep the research depth.
options.worked: Dense beats that stay with one object read well.
options.weaknesses: 97 sentences over 25 words; hedged; one primary quote (critique).

options.label: Short linted beats (40–100 words, ≤ 25-word sentences)
options.what: Content as YAML validated by zod and linted at build; quotes in Japanese with translation; confidence words.
options.why: Enforce the voice guide mechanically.
options.worked: Consistent, short, sourced; build fails on violations.
options.weaknesses: v3 read as fragments; v4 groups them into scenes on an ink thread.

options.label: Cast tables by role
options.what: Role tables with dates and what the learner needs.
options.why: Capture the whole cast, publisher first.
options.worked: Complete (58 documented).
options.weaknesses: No faces or story.

options.label: Role tabs with text cards
options.what: Five role tabs over dark name cards with kanji, dates and a note.
options.why: Show the cast by function.
options.worked: Puts carvers and the state in the cast.
options.weaknesses: No portraits; detached from lectures.

options.label: Inline cast card at first mention
options.what: A small card (portrait, kanji, dates, one line, credit) in the beat where a person first appears.
options.why: Meet people in context.
options.worked: Simple, in context.
options.weaknesses: v2: same 96×120 crop decapitates seated portraits; repeated portraits; thin cast.

options.label: Entity sheet dialog
options.what: A panel for a person/place/event/image with "Appears in" links.
options.why: Depth on demand.
options.worked: Shared component for all entity kinds.
options.weaknesses: Generic; not a character.

options.label: Character chip → card → sheet + Cast deck
options.what: Chips in prose (portrait or hanko), hover card, sheet with Story · Works · Connections · Life and "Show on map/timeline"; a Cast deck with unmet silhouettes and a met counter.
options.why: Main people as interactive character cards (brief).
options.worked: Strong, consistent, reusable; links people to instruments.
options.weaknesses: Met counter edges toward collection mechanics; needs portraits for all main people.

options.label: Atlas node card
options.what: Person as a node with making, confidence and "why this mark" edges.
options.why: Cross-chapter graph.
options.worked: Honest provenance.
options.weaknesses: Thin as a portrait of a person.

options.label: Maps specified, not drawn
options.what: I4, I6 and I9 describe the maps.
options.weaknesses: No map.

options.label: Schematic place diagram
options.what: Labelled pills in a Japan box and a world box with arc counts.
options.why: Stand in for a MapLibre build.
options.worked: Shows intent.
options.weaknesses: No geography.

options.label: d3 world dots + 1859 raster with pins by eye
options.what: Pacific-centred world (50 m), Japan and Kantō views, the LoC 1859 sheet as a raster with ten pins.
options.why: Put a world map beside the story.
options.worked: The blue route arc beat worked.
options.weaknesses: Decorative in 22 of 33 beats; Kantō a blob; Tōkaidō straight through Fuji; judged "should be an interactive world map".

options.label: Three-scale ink map (world, Japan/Kantō, georeferenced Edo)
options.what: Equal Earth world rotated per scene, Japan and Kantō on a 10 m coastline, Edo on the 1859 sheet with a fitted georeference; v4 adds place cards, label priority, relocation arcs, map guesses and Rebuild tiles.
options.why: Make the map do work in every map beat; scale breaks as their own beat.
options.worked: Accurate, legible, one ink style; city animations (fire, relocations).
options.weaknesses: City raster still a single sheet; no 1677 comparison yet.

options.label: Paper-and-ink 3D globe with 2D fallback
options.what: three.js globe with washes, routes and clustered marks; Equal Earth SVG fallback; list view.
options.why: "Atlas should be an interactive world map" (v2 critique) and the 3D study.
options.worked: Distinctive; honest about placement.
options.weaknesses: Hub-scale; not a teaching instrument inside the unit.

options.label: Era table + event list
options.what: Six eras and 78 sourced events as tables.
options.why: Capture the spine.
options.worked: Complete.
options.weaknesses: Not visual.

options.label: Proportional era bands + event chips
options.what: Six bands sized by years, afterlife folded, tap a chip for a node card.
options.why: Time as one of four lenses.
options.worked: Simple and clear.
options.weaknesses: No quantities or lanes.

options.label: Year scrubber inside a tool
options.what: Drag a year (1835–1850) and watch genres fade (Ban); scrub the blue route.
options.why: Make change over time tangible.
options.worked: Direct manipulation.
options.weaknesses: Separate from the main timeline; v2 versions autoplay.

options.label: Proportional ruler with folded afterlife
options.what: 1600–2024 strip, break after 1870, 33 events, ≤ 3 lit.
options.why: Always-visible time.
options.worked: Shows where you are.
options.weaknesses: "A ruler with 3 px knobs"; overlapping labels; no lanes (critique); judged should be designed like a timeline with animations.

options.label: Lane chart of the trade
options.what: Lanes by kind, lifespans, censor bands, price lane with the 1842 cap, print-run bubbles; mini strip under other stages. v4 adds a "now" cursor that inks the past and makes events happen, plus drag guesses and Rebuild tiles.
options.why: "A chart of the trade, not a ruler."
options.worked: Quantities and regimes visible; v4 animation answers the critique.
options.weaknesses: Dense on phones; needs careful labelling.
requires: timeline.yaml with lanes, bands, price, runs

options.label: Deep-time scrubber with play
options.what: 12,000 BCE–2026 with play; routes draw by year.
options.why: Cross-chapter time.
options.worked: Simple control for a hub.
options.weaknesses: Coarse for a unit.
